en.title: Equal-Stride Permutation Matching
en.description:
Given two strings and a positive stride p, count the start indices i such that the m characters at positions i, i+p, …, i+(m−1)p of the first string form a permutation of the second string. All indices must be in range.

The standard input format, examples and test data were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains userID1, the second line userID2, and the third line p. On this site the input consists of lowercase English letters; 1≤m≤n≤1000000, 1≤p≤1000000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: the valid starts are 0 and 2 (0-indexed), which take a, a, c at indices 0, 2, 4 and a, c, a at indices 2, 4, 6, both permutations of aac; the other start that can take all three characters, 1, gives c, c, a, which does not match, so the answer is 2. Example 2: the target has only one character, so the stride never produces a second index, and the only start 0 matches a. Example 3: a two-character target needs the start and start+2, which always goes out of range, so the answer is 0.
hints: Split the indices into chains by index mod p; on each chain, maintain a sliding window of length m with its character frequencies and compare them with the target frequencies.
